blueprint-comprehension.description: Reads an Unreal Engine Blueprint as NodeToCode's N2C JSON through the NodeToCode MCP tools and explains what it does: events, functions, execution order, data flow, variables and the nodes that never run. Use when the user asks what a Blueprint or one of its graphs does, wants it explained, summarized, reviewed, debugged or documented, or wants it read before editing, translating or migrating it; when a tool result holds N2C JSON ("version": "2.0.0", nodes, pins, flows.execution, flows.data); or when the user names a Blueprint asset such as /Game/Characters/BP_Hero. SKIP for: writing C++ from a Blueprint (use blueprint-to-cpp), moving a Blueprint's logic into C++ (use blueprint-migration), materials, and adding or wiring nodes.

blueprint-migration.description: Moves an Unreal Engine Blueprint's logic into a C++ class one Blueprint at a time, with review gates: inventory the Blueprint through the NodeToCode MCP tools, agree a plan, write and compile the C++ class, then, only after the user approves, reparent the Blueprint to it and remove the Blueprint logic the C++ now does. Use when the user wants to migrate, convert or move Blueprints (or a Blueprint-heavy feature) to C++, replace a Blueprint with a native base class, or 'nativize' gameplay code for performance or maintainability. SKIP for: explaining a Blueprint (use blueprint-comprehension), producing C++ from a graph without changing the project's Blueprints (use blueprint-to-cpp), and bulk conversion of many Blueprints in one pass.

blueprint-to-cpp.description: Translates Unreal Engine Blueprint graphs into Unreal C++ (.h and .cpp) from NodeToCode's N2C JSON: export the graph through the NodeToCode MCP tools, translate it yourself or with NodeToCode's translate tool, place the code in the project's module and compile it. Use when the user asks to convert, port, rewrite or translate a Blueprint, a Blueprint function or event graph to C++, wants the C++ equivalent of a Blueprint, asks for NodeToCode's own translator (translate-focused-blueprint, translate-batch), wants a tagged set of graphs exported or translated in one batch, or hands you N2C JSON to turn into code. SKIP for: only explaining a Blueprint (use blueprint-comprehension), replacing a Blueprint with a C++ class in the project, reparenting or removing Blueprint logic (use blueprint-migration), and languages other than C++.
